comparison.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop before repeated actuation; PR-1501 seats a click-type torque wrench on a busbar-lug bolt and tightens only to its calibrated click.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate coordinates a hex driver and open-ended wrench to oppose locknut reaction without moving an adjustment; PR-1501 requires socket seating and force termination at a one-shot break-over cue without under- or over-torquing.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate grades retained opening angle, nut seating, three-cycle drift, release, and tool clearance; PR-1501 grades full socket seating, click occurrence, 90–110% peak torque, absence of unseated turning/back-off, and released stillness.
comparison.reason: PR-1501 tests calibrated torque-cue response on one fastener, whereas the candidate tests preservation and functional retention of an adjustable setpoint while locking a coupled screw/nut pair. All versions specify numeric thresholds; no material rubric detail is missing.

review_notes: Busbar bolt click torque wrench, all versions: torque threshold versus preserving coupled adjustment.
